section_summary: This section consists chiefly of 1934 State Department correspondence, embassy and consular reports, newspaper clippings, and cross-reference sheets concerning Japanese-linked narcotics trafficking in East Asia and beyond. It documents seizures, arrests, smuggling routes, and court outcomes involving opium, heroin, morphine, cocaine, and benzyl morphine, alongside Chinese anti-drug campaigns and a Japanese association for treating addicts. The later records follow alleged trafficker Katsutoshi Tsunemitsu and the surveillance of pharmaceutical executive Hajime Hoshi during his journey through the United States.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Chinese newspaper articles on narcotics
subfiles.about: Forwards three Chinese newspaper articles concerning Japanese participation in narcotics traffic and an anti-drug campaign in Beijing.
subfiles.summary: State sends Treasury Peiping Chronicle and Peking and Tientsin Times articles of March 1934 on narcotics, for the Acting Commissioner of Narcotics.

subfiles.title: Japanese in the Dope-Drug Trade
subfiles.about: Describes widespread drug addiction in Harbin and alleges that Japanese- and Korean-run shops openly manufacture, sell, and facilitate the use of narcotics.
subfiles.summary: Article on Harbin as a major narcotics center: Russian families lack help for addicted sons, and a nominal pharmacy sells drugs and runs a smoking room; police allegedly leave such places undisturbed.

subfiles.title: 16 Arrests Made in Drug Factory Raid in Peiping
subfiles.about: Reports the raid of a disguised heroin factory in Beijing and the arrest of proprietor Liu Jung-hsiang and his workers.
subfiles.summary: Police raided a house inside Hepingmen registered as an Incomparable-brand tooth-powder business and seized roughly 1,000 ounces of heroin. The operation allegedly concealed heroin in tooth-powder packages and had received a shipment from Tianjin. The prisoners were to be transferred to the Beijing District Court.

subfiles.title: Anti-Drug Campaign
subfiles.about: Describes a Chinese government campaign against addiction among public employees and the broader growth of opium and heroin traffic.
subfiles.summary: Beijing departments ordered to identify and treat addicted employees, contrasted with opium monopolies, poppy growing and heroin manufacture; Japanese and Koreans allegedly smuggle extensively.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Kokumin Shimbun article
subfiles.about: Forwards a translation concerning the arrest of an alleged opium-smuggling leader in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Narcotics Commissioner a translation of a June 14 Kokumin Shimbun article on a bus chauffeur said to head a large smuggling organization.

subfiles.title: Chauffeur of 'Green Bus' Is Chief of Opium Smugglers
subfiles.about: Reports the arrest of pseudonymous chauffeur Katsushige Nakaya as the alleged chief of an opium-smuggling network.
subfiles.summary: Inspector Kobari arrested Nakaya in Tokyo after coordinating with Karafuto police; the network had contacts in Korea, Manchukuo and Taiwan and recruited steamer crews.

subfiles.title: Illicit Sale of Opium in Chosen: Principal Men Arrested
subfiles.doc_type: Translated newspaper article with Japanese original
subfiles.about: Reports arrests in Osaka connected with morphine supplied to an illicit Korean opium-selling group.
subfiles.summary: Police arrested Eiji Yanagimoto and a broker calling himself E. Minamiyama after tracing morphine found during an earlier raid in Daegu. The morphine bore the mark of the Dai Nippon Pharmaceutical Company and was allegedly shipped to Korea through Yanagimoto. Another alleged gang member, Minematsu, fled his Osaka hiding place.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: San Francisco seizures implicating Miyahara and Mase
subfiles.about: Refers to records concerning two San Francisco narcotics seizures involving Yahachiro Miyahara and Heigoro Mase.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: cocaine and morphine seized in San Francisco June 26 and 28 (Miyahara and Mase) may have come from Japan; notify Japanese authorities.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Osaka Asahi item on morphine traffic
subfiles.about: Forwards an Osaka Asahi report on Japanese investigation of morphine shipped from Osaka to Korea.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Narcotics Commissioner a translation of the June 18 Osaka Asahi item, drawing attention to the mark on the seized morphine.

subfiles.title: Opium Seized in Singapore
subfiles.about: Reports the seizure of opium concealed aboard a Blue Funnel steamship arriving in Singapore from Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Police boarded a ship and found opium behind smoking-room wainscoting at Singapore, worth £1,500.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Drug seizure from Chinese magistrate at Changli
subfiles.about: Refers to a mail report on a Japanese seizure of drugs from a Chinese magistrate at Changli.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram 1 in file 893.114 Narcotics/795 on a drug seizure from a Chinese magistrate at Changli.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 344: Conviction of Sennosuke Asai for Smuggling 4,292 Kilogrammes of Benzyl Morphine
subfiles.about: Reports the Osaka conviction and sentence of Sennosuke Asai for a major benzyl-morphine smuggling scheme.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 344: Amagasaki dance-hall owner Sennosuke Asai, a Kitada associate, convicted of importing 4,292 kilograms of benzyl morphine from Hamburg; enormous fine dischargeable by a year in prison; he appealed.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmittal of Asai despatch
subfiles.about: Confidentially forwards the Kobe despatch on Sennosuke Asai to the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: Confidentially transmits Despatch No. 344 on Asai's conviction, noting his association with Katsutoshi Tsunemitsu, number 33 on the Narcotics Confidential List.

subfiles.title: Instruction to report on Tsunemitsu
subfiles.from: U.S. Secretary of State, Cordell Hull
subfiles.about: Orders a full mailed report on the Osaka narcotics case involving Tsunemitsu.
subfiles.summary: Consul in Shanghai is told to ask the Tokyo Embassy for a full report on Tsunemitsu's arrest and inform Nicholson.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 950: Japanese Association for the Relief of Narcotics Addicts
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards a Japanese pamphlet describing an association devoted to treating narcotics addicts and expanding its operations.
subfiles.summary: Grew encloses a Japanese pamphlet on the Association for the Relief of Narcotics Addicts: 3,700 addicts in Osaka in 1929, 3,000 in Tokyo in 1932, mostly Korean laborers.

subfiles.title: Prospectus and Regulations of the Association for the Relief of Narcotics Addicts
subfiles.from: Association for the Relief of Narcotics Addicts
subfiles.about: Sets out the association's regulations, officers, treatment work, finances, statistics, and expansion plans.
subfiles.summary: The prospectus describes increasing addiction in Japan and Korea, the absence of adequate public relief regulations, and the association's establishment in Tokyo in 1933. It lists its officers and organizational rules and explains a withdrawal-and-labor treatment program at its first relief station. Statistics cover admissions and discharges through May 1934, while an expansion plan proposes facilities on Izu Ōshima capable of treating about 500 people annually.
keywords: Association for the Relief of Narcotics Addicts

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Wong Sow Eng seizure at Trinidad
subfiles.about: Refers to the Trinidad seizure of drugs of Japanese origin from Wong Sow Eng.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Wong Sow Eng's seizure at Trinidad of drugs allegedly of Japanese origin (844g.114 Narcotics/29).

subfiles.title: Trinidad Customs Authorities Seize Opium Valued at $24,000
subfiles.from: Alfredo L. Demorest, American Vice Consul, Trinidad
subfiles.about: Reports the arrest and conviction of Chinese steward Wong Sow Eng for attempting to land Japanese-manufactured opium in Trinidad.
subfiles.summary: Trinidad customs found six one-pound opium tins in a canvas waistcoat aboard the Cape Horn, valued at $24,000; Wong was imprisoned.

subfiles.title: Transmittal on addicts' relief association to Public Health Service
subfiles.to: U.S. Secretary of the Treasury, for the U.S. Public Health Service
subfiles.about: Forwards the Tokyo despatch and pamphlet translation concerning the Japanese addicts' relief association.
subfiles.summary: State sends Despatch No. 950 and the partial translation to the Public Health Service; another copy goes to the Narcotics Commissioner.

subfiles.title: Transmittal on addicts' relief association to Commissioner of Narcotics
subfiles.to: U.S. Secretary of the Treasury, for the Commissioner of Narcotics
subfiles.about: Forwards the Tokyo despatch and translated pamphlet concerning Japanese treatment of narcotics addicts.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Narcotics Commissioner Despatch No. 950 and translation; a copy also goes to the Public Health Service.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 598 requesting future reports on the relief association
subfiles.about: Requests continued reporting on the Japanese Association for the Relief of Narcotic Addicts and addiction in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 598 asks for future reports on the addicts' relief association and other information on narcotics addiction in Japan.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment of Despatch No. 950
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of material on the Japanese Association for the Relief of Narcotics Addicts.
subfiles.summary: Treasury confirms receipt of Tokyo Despatch No. 950 and the translated pamphlet for the Public Health Service.

subfiles.title: Telegram reporting issuance of a visa to Hajime Hoshi
subfiles.about: Reports Hajime Hoshi's visitor visa and planned transit through the United States despite his prior narcotics-related indictment.
subfiles.summary: Embassy reports Hajime Hoshi, Hoshi Pharmaceutical president, was indicted in 1933 for bribing revenue officers but not convicted; due in San Francisco November 7, sailing from New York November 23.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmittal of Hoshi visa telegram
subfiles.about: Confidentially forwards the Tokyo report concerning Hajime Hoshi's visitor visa.
subfiles.summary: Department sends the Narcotics Commissioner three paraphrase copies identifying Hoshi as suspected of complicity in illicit narcotics traffic.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Tokyo telegram concerning Hajime Hoshi
subfiles.about: Summarizes Hajime Hoshi's background, visitor visa, and intended U.S. itinerary.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase on Hoshi: former narcotics-trafficking suspect who escaped conviction on a bribery charge, arriving at San Francisco and leaving New York on the Conte di Savoia.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 384: Arrest of Narcotics Smugglers at Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports the arrest of a large group accused of smuggling narcotics from Japan to the United States and Asian destinations.
subfiles.summary: Hyogo police arrested alleged smugglers whose operations extended from 1929 through 1931. Donovan says the evidence appeared conclusive although no trial had yet occurred. He encloses Governor Takesuke Shirane's detailed account and promises a later report on the court's decision.

subfiles.title: Governor Shirane's account of the Kobe narcotics-smuggling group
subfiles.from: Takesuke Shirane, Governor of Hyogo Prefecture
subfiles.about: Identifies nine alleged smugglers and details shipments of cocaine, heroin, and morphine to foreign ports.
subfiles.summary: Shirane lists the suspects' ages, occupations, and addresses and describes seven shipments organized by Shigeo Kawasaki and associates. Other transactions allegedly carried narcotics to Tacoma, Bombay, Belawan, and Sinuiju aboard Osaka Shosen Kaisha ships. The case had been referred to the Kobe Local Court for expected indictment and trial.

subfiles.title: Jehol Opium Ring and Smugglers' Headquarters in the Tianjin Japanese Concession
subfiles.about: Presents competing Chinese and Japanese accusations concerning organized opium smuggling from Jehol through North China.
subfiles.summary: Reports allege Tianjin Japanese Concession rings bought Jehol opium under armed protection, and arrested peddlers accused Chinese officials of arranging a 45-case shipment; Japanese military denied involvement.

subfiles.title: Editorial on North China opium-smuggling accusations
subfiles.about: Comments on mutual Chinese and Japanese recriminations over smuggling Jehol opium across the Great Wall.
subfiles.summary: Editorial: Chinese believe customs exemptions for Japanese military stores hid smuggling; uninspected privileged shipments encouraged rumors, though the army is not accused of conspiracy.

subfiles.title: Drug Dealers Massacred
subfiles.about: Reports a Chinese official's claim that villagers killed Korean heroin dealers after an intimidation and extortion attempt.
subfiles.summary: Korean drug dealers and associates threatened villagers at Fushanssu, were driven off and massacred; Korean representatives in Tianjin sought bodies, punishment and compensation.

subfiles.title: Aeroplanes Used for Drug Smuggling
subfiles.about: Alleges that aircraft distributed opium and heroin from Guizhou through Hunan into Guangdong and Guangxi.
subfiles.summary: Chinese reports claimed drug shipments were flown from Hongjiang to southern provinces; General Huang Fei of the Hunan Air Corps was arrested.

subfiles.title: Drug Dealer's Last Speech and Chinese League Delegate's Review
subfiles.about: Reports a heroin dealer's execution in Beijing and Victor Hoo's defense of China's anti-narcotics policies before the League of Nations.
subfiles.summary: Drug dealer Feng Jui's last confession before execution, and Victor Hoo's Geneva reply on China's penalties, compulsory treatment and poppy suppression.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 995: Tsunemitsu, Alleged Drug Trafficker
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports preliminary findings on Katsutoshi Tsunemitsu's Osaka prosecution.
subfiles.summary: Osaka Chief Public Procurator Ryohei Wada identified Tsunemitsu as an accomplice of Sennosuke Asai and a comparatively minor member of the smuggling gang. His preliminary examination had ended and trial had begun, but no decision had yet been reached. The Embassy promised to report further developments.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmittal of Despatch No. 995
subfiles.about: Forwards the Tokyo despatch on Katsutoshi Tsunemitsu to the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: The Department sends duplicate copies of Despatch No. 995. It identifies Tsunemitsu as number 33 on the Narcotics Confidential List.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmittal of Despatch No. 384
subfiles.about: Forwards the Kobe report and enclosure on a group accused of international narcotics smuggling.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Despatch No. 384 and Governor Shirane's enclosure on narcotics traffic from Japan to the US and Asia, 1929-1933.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Raigorodetsky and Beerbrayer
subfiles.about: Refers to information on the last known addresses of two suspected narcotics traffickers.
subfiles.summary: The sheet identifies Raigorodetsky and Beerbrayer as suspects connected with illicit narcotics traffic. It directs the reader to letter 081.94/120.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1011: Drug Smuggling Activities of a Member of the Crew of the Manila Maru
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports investigation of possible narcotics smuggling by members of the Manila Maru's crew.
subfiles.summary: A press report linked a crew assault to a possible dispute over profits from opium smuggling, prompting an Embassy inquiry through the Kobe consulate. Kobe police found evidence only against Sekiyama Kawashige, who had already been convicted in Singapore. Grew encloses both the newspaper translation and Howard Donovan's investigative report.

subfiles.title: Osaka Asahi report on the Manila Maru investigation
subfiles.about: Reports a police search of the Manila Maru after allegations of crew involvement in large-scale opium smuggling.
subfiles.summary: Osaka Asahi: Kobe Water Police searched the Manila Maru crew at Moji after an assault on the chief steward and steward Sekiyama's Singapore conviction.

subfiles.title: Consular report on Sekiyama Kawashige and the Manila Maru
subfiles.to: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports that police found no Manila Maru narcotics conspiracy beyond Kawashige's individual offense.
subfiles.summary: Chief Detective Hayashi says Kawashige carried opium to Singapore and was already punished abroad, and the assault on the chief steward was personal hostility.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Sherwood Eddy article on the opium traffic
subfiles.about: Refers to an enclosed and annotated article by Dr. Sherwood Eddy about the opium traffic.
subfiles.summary: The sheet directs the reader to File 893.114 Narcotics/885. The referenced article itself is not reproduced on this page.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmittal of Despatch No. 1011
subfiles.about: Forwards the Embassy report and enclosures on a Manila Maru crewman's drug-smuggling activities.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Narcotics Commissioner Despatch No. 1011 on the opium-smuggling case involving a Manila Maru crew member.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Proposed Formosa–Amoy opium transaction
subfiles.about: Refers to a report of a large opium transaction allegedly under negotiation between the Formosan government and an Amoy combine.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: a proposed Formosa-Amoy opium transaction led by Yip San Ho (Paul Yip) and implicating Chen Chang Foo.

subfiles.title: Treasury report on Hajime Hoshi's arrival in San Francisco
subfiles.about: Reports Hajime Hoshi's arrival, onward travel, and possession of undeclared cocaine.
subfiles.summary: Hoshi arrived at San Francisco November 7 and left for Los Angeles and Chicago; customs seized a quarter-ounce cocaine bottle lacking a permit.

subfiles.title: Bureau of Narcotics report on Hajime Hoshi in San Francisco
subfiles.from: D. A. Bagley, Acting District Supervisor
subfiles.to: H. J. Anslinger, Commissioner of Narcotics
subfiles.about: Details surveillance of Hajime Hoshi during his San Francisco stopover and arrangements to continue monitoring him.
subfiles.summary: Agents Roberts and Carli watched Hoshi, recorded contacts, seized his cocaine and noted his rail itinerary to New York.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 393: Arrest and Conviction of Narcotics Smugglers at Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports the sentences imposed on four members of the Kobe narcotics-smuggling group.
subfiles.summary: Shigeo Kawasaki and Giichiro Asahi received three months' penal servitude, while Shoji Takahashi and Kanjo Yugi received one month, with pretrial detention credited. Five other detained suspects were not indicted. Donovan characterizes the sentences as extremely nominal and cites a broader pattern of judicial leniency in Japanese narcotics cases.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmittal of Despatch No. 393
subfiles.about: Forwards the Kobe despatch reporting sentences for international narcotics smuggling.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Narcotics Commissioner Despatch No. 393 on a group active 1929-1933 in traffic to the US and Asia.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1044: Tsunemitsu, Alleged Trafficker in Narcotic Drugs
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards the latest Kobe consular report on Katsutoshi Tsunemitsu's Osaka case.
subfiles.summary: Grew refers to the earlier departmental instruction and Embassy Despatch No. 995. He encloses Howard Donovan's November 2 report describing Tsunemitsu's conviction and appeal.

subfiles.title: Consular report and translated judgment in the Tsunemitsu case
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Tsunemitsu's conviction, sentence, smuggling quantities, and appeal.
subfiles.summary: Osaka court convicted Tsunemitsu October 25 for smuggling benzyl and benzol morphine from Germany with Kitada and Asai: three months' servitude, ¥111,000 fine; large fines dischargeable by short imprisonment.

subfiles.title: Treasury report of Hajime Hoshi's departure for Europe
subfiles.about: Reports Hoshi's departure from New York and plans for continued monitoring in Europe.
subfiles.summary: Treasury says Hoshi sailed from New York November 23 on the Conte di Savoia; its Paris representative was told to check his European movements.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of New York reports on Hajime Hoshi
subfiles.from: F. A. Birgfeld for the U.S. Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards Bureau of Narcotics reports concerning Hajime Hoshi's activities in New York City.
subfiles.summary: Treasury sends New York reports supplementing its earlier ones on Hoshi's US transit and November 23 departure.

subfiles.title: Forwarding memorandum on Hajime Hoshi
subfiles.about: Forwards Harold C. McKenney's additional report on Hajime Hoshi.
subfiles.summary: Igoe states that the enclosure supplements his November 23 report. Two copies of McKenney's additional investigative report are transmitted.

subfiles.title: Narcotic Agent McKenney's report on Hajime Hoshi in New York
subfiles.about: Records Hoshi's communications, shipments, press contact, and New York office connections.
subfiles.summary: Narcotic Agent McKenney reports Hoshi's contacts in Philadelphia, Osaka and Tokyo and his company sharing office space at 56 Pine Street with the Hosken Trading Company.

subfiles.title: Traffic in Narcotics—Japan: Case 200 jacket
subfiles.about: Identifies the file jacket for the Japan narcotics-traffic case.
subfiles.summary: File jacket: Traffic in Narcotics-Japan, case 200.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmittal of Despatch No. 1044
subfiles.about: Forwards the Tokyo despatch and enclosure on Katsutoshi Tsunemitsu.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Narcotics Commissioner Despatch No. 1044 with a Kobe enclosure; Tsunemitsu again noted as number 33 on the Confidential List.

subfiles.title: Instruction transmitting notice of Hajime Hoshi's departure
subfiles.about: Notifies the Tokyo consulate that Hajime Hoshi departed the United States on November 23.
subfiles.summary: Instruction encloses Treasury's November 28 letter reporting Hoshi's departure from New York on the Conte di Savoia.
